title: Establishment of an indication for radiation therapy for thymus tumors based on the 9th edition of the TNM classification
summary:
Background
Thymus tumors are rare cancers of the gland in the chest. After complete surgical removal of the tumor, it is clear which patients will benefit from additional radiation (postoperative radiation therapy). However, since the classification of tumor stages has changed, the recommendation for radiation must be reviewed for the new classification. In order to improve treatment recommendations for the future and to include them in the international standard work on cancer stages (9th TNM classification), data from as many patients as possible worldwide must be analyzed.

Research question
The study investigates whether radiation therapy after complete tumor removal reduces the risk of recurrence and improves the long-term survival chances of patients. The aim is to establish clear criteria for when such radiation therapy is medically appropriate and when it can be omitted.

Methodology
This is a global, retrospective study for which data from over 50 institutions is being collated. The study analyzes the disease progression of patients (over 18 years of age) whose tumors were completely removed between 2000 and 2025. It compares progression with and without subsequent radiation therapy. The study will collect data from several hundred cases until the end of 2025 in order to be able to make statistically reliable statements about recurrence-free survival and overall survival.

interventions.name: R0 Patients who have undergone surgery without adjuvant radiation therapy are compared with R0 patients who have undergone surgery with adjuvant radiation therapy. The surgery therefore takes place at the very beginning of the observation period, followed by radiation therapy or no radiation therapy

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients with thymoma, neuroendocrine thymic tumor, thymic carcinoma, histologically determined
Surgery with RO resection of the tumor
Postoperative radiation therapy (PORT) and no PORT
The following classifications are available: WHO subtype classification, Masaoka-Koga classification, TNM classification for tumor available, with only Masaoka-Koga classification stages 1-3 considered
Exclusion criteria:
Surgery with R1/R2 tumor residue
Neoadjuvant or palliative radiation therapy
Direct evidence of distant metastases
Severe concomitant medical conditions or other contraindications for PORT
